utility.notes: SCE's own 'Incorporated Cities and Counties Served by SCE' fact sheet (updated 3/17/2025) explicitly lists 'San Jacinto' by name among the cities in its service area.

generation_supplier.notes: San Jacinto is not a Western Community Energy member city (Eastvale, Hemet, Jurupa Valley, Norco, Perris, and Wildomar are); WCE itself deregistered with the CPUC and dissolved via Chapter 9 bankruptcy in 2021. No CCA was found serving San Jacinto this session.

permit_authority.value: City of San Jacinto Community Development Department, Building & Safety Division

interconnection_url.notes: SCE's own Net Energy Metering (NEM) program page — a utility-wide fact already established for other SCE-territory records this session.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Southern California Edison (SCE), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by SCE across its entire distribution territory, which includes San Jacinto/Riverside County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC-administered SGIP program already confirmed for other SCE-territory records this session, reused as a utility-level fact.

timeline_days.notes: The page states the Instant Solar Permit 'instantly' issues a permit for code-compliant systems but does not give a specific day-range figure.

other_conditions: Only for use by contractors registered with SolarAPP+
Covers roof-mounted solar photovoltaic panel installations with or without an energy storage system
A main electrical service upgrade can be added to the Instant Solar Permit
Only systems included on the SolarAPP+ Eligibility Checklist lists are eligible
